questions.prompt: What is the cell membrane mainly made of?
options: A double layer of phospholipids with proteins inside
A single sheet of rigid cellulose
Pure water with no structure
A mixture of DNA and sugar
questions.explanation: The membrane is a phospholipid bilayer - two rows of oily molecules with the heads facing water and the tails tucked inward - with proteins floating in it, forming a flexible yet organized sheet.
questions.misconception: It is tempting to imagine a hard shell, but the membrane is a flexible, fluid-like double layer of lipids, not a stiff wall.

questions.prompt: What does 'selective permeability' mean for a cell membrane?
options: It lets some substances pass but blocks others
It lets everything through freely
It lets nothing in or out at all
It only lets lipids through and nothing else
questions.explanation: Selective means the membrane chooses: small, simple molecules like water pass through; larger or charged ones need special protein doors, giving the cell control over its inside.
questions.misconception: Some assume 'selective' means 'leaks things or blocks everything.' The truth is it is a controlled filter - some things move freely, some need help, some are kept out.

questions.prompt: Which molecule can most easily pass straight through the lipid bilayer on its own?
options: A small water molecule
A large protein
A big starch molecule
A heavy salt particle
questions.explanation: Small, simple molecules like water pass through the bilayer because they are small enough to slip between the lipid tails. Large or charged particles usually need protein doors.
questions.misconception: People sometimes think any needed 'stuff' passes freely. Size and charge matter - the tiny water molecule goes through easily, the big or charged ones do not.

questions.prompt: Which is true about the cell membrane?
options: Every cell has a cell membrane
Only plant cells have a cell membrane
Only animal cells have a cell membrane
Cells in water do not need a membrane
questions.explanation: All cells - animal, plant, and bacterial - are wrapped in a cell membrane. It is the boundary that makes each cell a separate unit with control over its insides.
questions.misconception: Because plants also have a cell wall, some people think plants lack a membrane too. In fact the plant cell has BOTH a membrane (inside) and a wall (outside).

questions.prompt: How is the cell membrane different from a plant cell wall?
options: The membrane controls entry and exit; the wall mainly gives support and shape
The membrane is thick and rigid; the wall controls entry
They are the same structure with two names
The membrane only exists in animal cells
questions.explanation: The membrane is thin, flexible, alive, and controls what crosses the boundary. The cell wall is thick and rigid and mainly provides structure and protection.
questions.misconception: The two are easily confused because they both wrap the cell. But function is different - the gate is on the membrane, while the wall is a sturdy, non-living shell.
